analysis.title: GS US TMT .. bounce back* ..
key_insights: The NDX ended a 4-week losing streak, closing up about 350 bps on the week. Semis/SOX rose about 800 bps, the best week since early August. Both NDX and SOX still closed below their 200-day moving averages on Friday.
Nvidia is down 12% YTD after its biggest week of underperformance relative to Semis since 2008. Unexpected NVDA headlines drove two-way debate. AMD and the ASIC ecosystem were strong in reaction.
US Financial Conditions rose to their tightest level in about 18 months after another hotter CPI print. 10-year yields are back at 5.15% and oil is near $96/brl.

The desk attributes last week's strength largely to cleaner positioning (GS PB data showed covering via macro products) and intra-market rotation into Defensives, Big Tech (including AMD and AVGO) and Low Vol names.

The desk sees relatively little consensus in the market, except for a broadly receptive tilt toward Hyperscalers. Debate centers on where we are in the AI/Semi cycle, what is priced in, and whether this is a bear market bounce or a bull market forming. The desk calls it a 'blank slate' on positioning and sentiment, and arguably a healthier landscape into 2027.
Software dispersion has picked up, including within Cyber and Data Infra. Internet has become squeezy and hard to trade, with some 'value' interest emerging.

Top client inbounds: why Tech/AI is bouncing so hard and whether it is sustainable, memory stack rankings (HDDs, DRAM, NAND), whether people are long or short AI/Semis, new Internet ideas (OTAs, UBER, NFLX, APP), the setup into the NVDA print, and why AMAT and CSCO fell so much T+1.

NVDA market cap is back below $4trn and now matches MSFT's. MDB, MSFT, DELL and TSM are testing their 50-day moving averages to the downside. ZS is lower on 12 of 14 days. EBAY and ETSY are up 6 of 7 weeks. Staples, Low Vol and Pharma continue to rally strongly. CMCSA and CHTR are 20-35% off their lows.

NVDA reports Tuesday 11/17 after the close. The stock has a 14-day RSI of 24, lowest since 2019, and trades at 11x NTM P/E, in line with FLEX, WFC, EXPE, PYPL and CTSH. Investor focus is expected on Vera Rubin momentum, 2027+ visibility, gross margins and capital allocation.

DIS reports Tuesday morning 11/17. The stock is re-testing the $120s level, which has acted as a ceiling for about 4+ years. Focus is on strategic initiatives into 2027+: cruise fleet expansion, theme park capex, the theatrical pipeline and the planned Spring 2027 Disney+ integration of merchandise and interactive features.

PANW reports Wednesday 11/18 after the close. The stock has been lower on 9 of 12 prints on T+1 and is back in the low $300s, about $100 off YTD highs. Sentiment remains upbeat because it is seen as a thematically 'right way' AI name. Focus is on signs of AI uplift as PANW starts to lap the CyberArk and Chronosphere acquisitions in 1Q C27.

INTU reports Thursday 11/19 after the close. Inbounds are very low, and the stock has not closed above its 200-day moving average in over a year. It is a 'show me' story, with focus on Intuit Intelligence, QuickBooks industry verticals and consumer touchpoints.

AAPL vs NDX is approaching highs. Investors are frustrated that bear points after Apple's recent earnings (Services growth deceleration, gross margin headwinds, AI unknowns including server-side inference costs) have not weighed on the stock.
SPX ex-AI has outperformed SPX over the last year and was more resilient in last week's sell-off.

GS's 2027 macro outlook expects global growth of 2.8% in 2027, as lower energy prices and strong AI capex outweigh tighter financial conditions and neutral fiscal policy. Risks are tilted to the downside: renewed Iran escalation, large fiscal deficits pushing up long-term yields (especially France), and AI capex disappointment. GS also sees early signs AI is weighing on the job market.

Calendar this week: Fed Chair Warsh speaks Mon 11/16 at 1pm ET, US Retail Sales Tue 11/17, FOMC Minutes Wed 11/18. Earnings include DIS, NVDA, PANW, INTU and ESTC. Events include SuperCompute, MSFT Ignite and the TTWO GTA VI launch on Thursday.
